thread:
Eve: FYI customer reported sudden 429s this morning after their monthly credits hit 0. They say reset didn’t happen at midnight local (Europe/Amsterdam) and instead happened ~2 hours earlier. ticket: #64231
Eve: Customer says they were mid-batch and streaming calls failed with 429 then resumed after a manual top-up. Wants to know when exactly monthly credits reset and whether transfers between orgs could shift the window.
Carlos: @Eve can you paste the customer’s org-id and the timezone they expect? I'll check billing windows.
Eve: org: acme-eu-12, timezone reported: Europe/Amsterdam. They attached a small repro: one long-running streaming session that consumed ~1.2M tokens.
Anika: Do we have any recent infra changes that could affect the quota roll or scheduled job? @Bret?
Bret: Not on infra schedule. The refill job runs off UTC midnight boundary for hosted customers, but we do translate presentation to org timezone for UI. We had a one-off deploy last week that changed a cron expression for a housekeeping job, not the refill.
Eve: Customer insists it used to reset at 00:00 local, now it felt like 22:00 previous day. They provided these log timestamps:
```
2026-11-14T21:58:03Z token_balance: 0.00 org=acme-eu-12
2026-11-14T22:01:12Z 429 start stream id=abc123
2026-11-14T22:02:00Z manual_topup 500000 tokens by support
2026-11-15T00:00:05+01:00 UI shows next refill: 2026-12-01T00:00:00+01:00
```
Eve: They think DST or a recent tenant transfer might have changed their effective window.
Carlos: Two thoughts: 1) For hosted accounts we run refill at UTC midnight and then apply org timezone offset only for display. 2) If the tenant was migrated between regions or from Dedicated -> Hosted, the refill anchor could have switched to UTC if migration wasn't backfilled.
Anika: Could the manual top-up have prevented the automatic refill from triggering if balance > 0 at UTC midnight?
Bret: Refill logic is: if current_balance < monthly_commit then set balance to monthly_commit at UTC midnight anchor. We do not subtract inflight tokens. If they had manual_topup to bump them above threshold before the job, it could skip. But their logs show balance 0 at 21:58Z then 22:02 manual_topup, so that doesn’t explain earlier-than-expected reset.
Eve: Customer: "We were watching and local midnight passed and nothing happened, then next morning it showed it had reset but with a timestamp that made it look earlier."
Anika: Hmm. Could be a presentation bug where the UI shows next-refill with org-local time but the actual anchor belongs to the billing account (which might be owned by a parent org in UTC). If their billing owner is in a different timezone, display may mislead.
Carlos: I'll check billing-owner timezone and whether this org was involved in any transfer. ETA 30m.
Eve: Quick repro steps the customer provided for us to validate in staging:
1) Create org with timezone Europe/Amsterdam
2) Consume credits until balance ~0 mid-evening UTC
3) Observe refill at UTC midnight and compare UI next-refill string
They included curl log showing epoch seconds for the API: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/acme-eu-12/balance` returning `{"balance":0,"next_refill":1700006400}` (epoch).
Bret: If we get the epoch we can decode it. 1700006400 => 2023-11-14T00:00:00Z-ish in their example but we'll decode real one.
deploy-bot: scheduled-job refill-run started at 1953043200Z (run-id: refill-2026-11-15-00)
deploy-bot: scheduled-job refill-run finished in 1.2s (affected 812 orgs)
Anika: deploy-bot shows the job ran at 1953043200Z which is 2026-11-15T00:00:00Z. That explains the anchor: we run at UTC. The UI should map next_refill to org local but if the display code subtracts DST incorrectly it can show an earlier local time.
Carlos: Found in billing: acme-eu-12 was migrated from an older billing account two months ago; parent billing timezone is UTC. Migration meta shows parent_owner: acme-parent (tz: UTC) and migration timestamp 2026-09-01T03:00:00Z.
Eve: Customer asks: will a tenant transfer change the monthly cycle day? They have a contract that expects local-month alignment.
Carlos: By design we currently keep the refill anchor aligned to UTC for hosted accounts; transfers do not preserve prior local offsets. We should have flagged this in migration notes. That's on us.
Bret: Short-term workaround: manual top-up to cover the remainder of the customer's window + set a reminder to revert after their local midnight. Long-term fix: option to set org refill anchor to local timezone per tenant and ensure migration preserves it.
Anika: I'll open a product ticket for timezone-aware anchors and a migration audit. @Carlos please add migration note to the ticket so we can track affected customers.
Eve: Customer is OK with manual top-up and wants confirmation we’ll add a migration flag to prevent unexpected anchor changes. Asking for ETA.
Carlos: I’ll propose a communications message and approve a one-off credit to compensate the unexpected window shift.
Eve: Thanks all — looping customer in with summary and interim top-up. Will follow up once product ticket is created. :thumbsup:
